sentences.text: Facts in brief are that a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 was filed by mother of deceased Maya Bai/appellant no. 1, father of deceased Ramsujan/appellant no. 2 and brother of deceased Satish Kumar Patel/appellant no. 3 for the compensation regarding death of Gudda Patel in an accident which occurred on 16th June, 2020 at 5:00 P.M. near village Rupond situated on Maihar Satna road by use of motorcycle bearing registration no. MP 54 MC 4234 driven by Mohd. Latif and insured by respondent no. 2 The United India Insurance Company Ltd. and owned by Mohd. Kasim.
The age of deceased Gudda Patel was stated to be 25 years at the time of the accident and his per month income was stated to be Rs. 38,000/- .
The Driver of the offending vehicle died in the incident and respondent no. 1 did not contest the case.
Respondent no. 2 contested the claim on the ground of contributory negligence and on the ground of quantum.

The learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal has framed the issues and recorded the evidence of Maya Bai as PW-1, Rohit Patel as PW-2, Shri Jitendra Singh Baghel Assistant Grade-II,
R.T.O. office, Katni as PW-3, Branch Manager State Bank of India Branch Vilayatkala Shri Abhishek Kumar as PW-4 and adduced Ex. P-1 to P-11.

entities.text: State Bank of India Branch Vilayatkala
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Respondent no. 2 adduced Ex. D-1 to Ex. D-11 and examined Rajesh Kumar Kuchya Investigator as DW-1 and Shri M.A. Xavier, Senior Assistant,
United India Insurance Company Ltd. as DW-2.

The learned Tribunal assessed the age of deceased Gudda Patel at the time of the accident to be 25 years and estimated per month income of deceased Gudda Patel as Rs. 28,000/- deducting half of the income for personal expenses and adding 50% enhancement for future prospects and calculated the loss of per month income of Rs. 21,000/- and applied the multiplier of 13 on the basis of age of father of deceased Ramsujan Patel.

The Tribunal calculated the total loss of dependency to be Rs.
32,76,000/- and awarded Rs. 1,35,000/- under the head of loss of consortium and Rs. 15,000/-
under the head of funeral expenses and awarded total compensation of Rs. 34,26,000/-.
This appeal has been preferred claiming enhancement of Rs. 3,00,000/- on the ground that the Tribunal has awarded the compensation on the lower side and many heads have not been considered.
Learned counsel for respondent no. 2 has opposed the prayer.
Perused the record.
The Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of loss of estate.

The Tribunal also committed an error applying the multiplier on the basis of age of father of the deceased whereas multiplier has to be applied on the basis of age of deceased Gudda Patel and on the basis of age of deceased Gudda Patel, multiplier of 18 is applicable.
Therefore, this appeal is allowed and Rs. 3,00,000/- is enhanced to the compensation already awarded by the Tribunal.
The respondent no. 2 shall also pay 6% interest on the enhanced amount from the date of application i.e. 6th July, 2020.
Rest of the conditions of the award shall be same as imposed by the Tribunal.
